title: Sub-extensive non-stabilizerness in the Dyck-Fredkin spin chain
abstract: The stabilizer Rényi entropy is a quantitative measure of non-stabilizerness, or magic, and has typically been found to scale extensively with system size $N$ (i.e., $Θ(N)$) for a variety of many-body quantum states. In this note, we study the stabilizer Rényi entropy of the ground state of the spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Dyck-Fredkin chain and its $t$-deformation, a local frustration-free model with unusual spectral-gap scaling. Exploiting the combinatorial structure, we carry out numerically exact finite-size calculations, which indicate asymptotic behavior depending on $t$: $Θ(N)$ for $t<1$, $Θ(\log N)$ at $t=1$, and $Θ(1)$ for $t>1$. The scaling at $t=1$ could be another manifestation of the unconventional criticality of the model, while the contrast with the behavior of the entanglement entropy suggests that non-stabilizerness might provide a new window into quantum many-body systems.
summary: This work analyzes the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) of the Dyck-Fredkin spin chain under a deformation parameter $t$. The SRE reveals three distinct scaling regimes—linear, logarithmic, and constant—depending on $t$. This demonstrates that non-stabilizerness can serve as a sensitive diagnostic tool, potentially offering new insights into quantum many-body criticality compared to entanglement entropy.
main_problem: The study investigates the scaling behavior of non-stabilizerness, quantified by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), in quantum many-body systems to probe their critical properties.
main_result: The SRE exhibits distinct scaling behaviors ($\Theta(N)$, $\Theta(\log N)$, or $\Theta(1)$) depending on the deformation parameter $t$, suggesting non-stabilizerness offers a unique diagnostic tool distinct from entanglement entropy.
method: The authors employ numerically exact finite-size calculations and asymptotic analysis on the SRE, which is derived from the ground state of the spin chain.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the spin-1/2 Dyck-Fredkin chain and its $t$-deformation, a local frustration-free model whose ground state is a weighted superposition of Dyck-path states.
key_observables: Stabilizer Rényi entropy ($\alpha$-SRE), entanglement entropy, and the spectral gap.
important_parameters: The deformation parameter $t$, which dictates three distinct scaling regimes: $t<1$, $t=1$, and $t>1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on exploiting the combinatorial structure of the ground state and performing asymptotic approximations for the normalization factor $C(t)$.
figures_summary: Figure 2 shows the $\alpha$-SRE scaling for the undeformed chain ($\log N$ scaling). Figure 3 illustrates the three distinct scaling regimes ($t<1$, $t=1$, $t>1$) for the deformed chain.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the SRE as a measure of non-stabilizerness, derives the necessary formulas using replica methods, and then performs numerical and asymptotic calculations to map the scaling behavior across the parameter $t$.
why_interesting: The clear distinction in scaling behavior ($\Theta(N)$ vs $\Theta(\log N)$ vs $\Theta(1)$) based on a simple parameter $t$ provides a powerful, quantifiable tool to characterize different types of quantum criticality beyond standard entanglement measures.
